# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 99 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 99 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_099_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 16

**1** "And the stones cropped all around that were thrown far from the tower — who are they?" I asked. **2** "These are those who believed but then departed from the way of truth," he said. "They are the worst of all in their sins, yet a small remnant of faith remains in them; because of this they were not utterly destroyed, but were thrown far away. **3** Yet repentance for them is not difficult; for they simply turned away from the truth without transgressing the commandment of God. Since the day they departed, however, they have lost what little faith they had." **4** "And the spotted ones — who are they?" **5** "These are those who came to faith and lived mostly in righteousness, but had some worldly attachment; therefore they are spotted and not whole." **6** "And those who were half-burned — who are they?" **7** "These are those who lived among the heathen and wavered as to whether to remain with the servants of God or with the heathen. They were burned in that they sinned to some degree; but since they did not wholly depart from God, they were not entirely consumed." **8** "And the cracked ones — who are they?" **9** "These are those who harbored evil thoughts against one another in their hearts and did not make peace among themselves; they maintained an outward appearance of peace, but when they separated from one another their wicked thoughts remained. **10** These cracks in their hearts are the cracks in the stones. Those who repented were healed — repentance restored those who were cracked." **11** "And those who returned the short stones — who are they?" "These were faithful, but they also had large measures of double-mindedness, and therefore fell short of the complete measure — they were short because they always had some worldly attachment in them."

---

### Translator's Note
The "half-burned" category (vv. 6-7) is one of Hermas's most acute social observations: believers poised between Christian community and pagan surroundings, partially singed but not consumed. The "cracked" stones as hidden resentment masked by outward peace (vv. 9-10) is psychologically sophisticated — the crack is inside, invisible until the stone is examined closely. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
